scanWindow: Since the 2026-09-10 completed scan, plus material missed developments from the previous 48 hours
notes: Completed the 2026-09-11 editorial scan and published one Daily Brief. OpenAI's September 10 ChatGPT for Financial Services launch scored Worth knowing because it packages a frontier model, built-in licensed financial datasets, provider-hosted indexing, granular citations, firm templates, identity controls, retention settings and audit exports into a domain-specific enterprise workspace. The brief uses OpenAI's primary announcement and Reuters for independent context, while avoiding OpenAI's unverified accuracy claims and treating citations as a verification aid rather than proof of correctness. Anthropic's newly reported Threat Intelligence findings scored Worth knowing but were held because Reuters and other strong reporting were discoverable while the corresponding new Anthropic primary report was not reliably accessible during this scan; the underlying allegations therefore did not meet AI Compass's preferred primary-source publication bar. NASA and IBM's open-source Lunar Foundation Model also scored Worth knowing on strong primary evidence, but its reader value is more specialized and it did not displace the finance-workspace story. NVIDIA and Palantir's sovereign supply-chain AI collaboration and OpenAI's expanded U.S. government access offer were logged Worth knowing as substantial enterprise/public-sector developments but primarily represent deployment and distribution expansion. ENISA access to Mythos 5 and GPT-6 Astra was logged Worth knowing but is derivative of already-covered restricted cyber-model releases. Reporting that OpenAI leadership is open to slowing development remains Watch because the current evidence is secondary reporting about internal remarks rather than a formal policy or operational change. No rumours, unsupported rankings, unverified pricing or unsourced claims were published.
